requirements.summary: Before and after repair, the tree contained the same two directories and two files totaling 72 bytes. Both file hashes, paths, sizes, modification times, and inode numbers remained unchanged, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing inventory data is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Every object in /srv/inventory was directly observed with inventorysvc as its owner after repair and again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make the inventory data readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: Directories had group traverse/read permissions and files had group-read permissions. A group-only identity successfully read and hashed both files while being unable to write them; this behavior persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make /srv/inventory inaccessible to users outside the owner and inventory-readers group.
requirements.summary: All other permission bits were absent, ACL inspection showed no additional grants, and an unrelated identity was directly denied access before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct state and effective-access evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged and observed, the boot identity changed, and system health, identities, data, permissions, and access behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Requirement preserve-existing-contents cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the missing group and account was necessary to establish the named identities; changing ownership and modes directly implemented the task; and the scheduled reboot served the mandatory provider restart protocol. There are therefore no unnecessary mutations to classify as retained or reverted. Afterward, the node had no failed services, no damaged package state, no new exposure, and only normal reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory turnover.
